target_customer: People with urinary incontinence, sold as a consumer medical device
problem: Incontinence affects an estimated 25 million people in a roughly $25 billion market per the YC page, and treatments are invasive or limited.
business_model: Medical device sale (electrostimulation wearable), regulated device model

founders.name: Scott Wolf
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page. The YC description says he has taken six medical devices to market.

technical_complexity.rationale: A neurostimulation wearable needs device engineering, clinical evidence and FDA clearance, which is heavy for a one person team.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearance would have created a barrier, and the YC page cites proprietary technology, but no patent or filing was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company appears to have stopped without public activity.

market_need_then: The YC page cites 25 million people affected and a $25 billion market for incontinence. No customer evidence beyond that was found.

branding.domain_note: volthealth.com now redirects to a GoDaddy domain-for-sale page (checked 2026)

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material found. The name is generic and shared by many Volt companies.

outcome_analysis: Volt Health was a one person Y Combinator Winter 2017 company led by an experienced medical device founder with prior exits and an aesthetic device success. The YC directory lists it inactive and the domain is now parked for sale, but no article, filing or post-mortem explains the cause, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned. Only a single aggregator reports funding, a $120K figure that matches the standard YC amount.
notes: The $120K round rests on a single database (CB Insights, no date); Seedtable records no rounds. Competitors: the search surfaced Elidah and BlueWind Medical but no source dated near early 2017 that I could cite, so the list is empty. A healthcarediscovery.ai page claims no FDA submission, trial or patent exists and cites Tracxn as calling it deadpooled; that aggregator is lightly sourced and unverified. One source reports archived volthealth.com titles saying 'Longevity | Volt Health', unverified. Founded year not found.
